# Coverage

Where everything in Lauren Tan's talk and her two pstack guide posts lives in this kit, plus every skill those skills reference. `node scripts/validate.mjs` fails if a skill in the kit is missing from the catalog, so this page cannot fall behind.

- 98 skills from 9 plugins, plus 3 dormant automation skills.
- 12 skills are named in the posts, and all of them are here.
- 27 ideas, bots, and tools from the talk and posts are mapped to the skills that carry them.

## Lauren Tan's talk on building trust in agents

It names no skill by name. Everything it describes is mapped below.

What it describes:

| Idea or tool | In this kit |
|---|---|
| Control Glass, the verification skill in the talk: it runs the app and takes traces | `/create-verification-skill` writes one for your repository; `control-ui`, `control-cli`, and `control-mobile` are the harness recipes it builds on |
| The feature map stored in the skill, and the automation that keeps it current | `/create-verification-skill` writes the map; `/maintain-verification-skill` on a daily routine from `setup-routines` keeps it current |
| The layers of trust: codebase, static analysis, rules and Bugbot, skills | `correct` routes each correction to the strongest layer; `trust-audit` scores a repository on each |
| Making mistakes impossible with data structures, types, and the framework | `paved-path`, the language `*-best-practices` skills, and `references/agent-friendly-architecture.md` |
| Dune, the agent-friendly framework | `paved-path` and `references/agent-friendly-architecture.md` |
| Linters, compiler diagnostics, and CI | The seven lint packs, `setup-lint-pack`, `encode-lint-rule`, `check-compiler-errors`, `fix-ci`, `loop-on-ci` |
| Rules | AGENTS.md and nested AGENTS.md templates from `setup-team-kit`; `correct` adds a rule when nothing stronger can hold it; `continual-learning` mines transcripts for more |
| Bugbot | `setup-review-bots` (Claude and Codex review on every PR), `thermos`, and pstack's `references/bugbot-triage.md` |
| Agents leaving comments to justify papering over a problem | `/no-comments`, the Comment Sicko agent, and the agnostic pack's `no-new-comments` check |
| A gardener who watches the codebase for spreading smells | `gardener`, with a daily routine template |
| Extracting what reviewers keep saying into the codebase: the style guide | `style-guide-from-reviews`, then `correct` to promote each entry down the ladder |
| Grok Bot routines that react to Slack threads and Sentry alerts | `setup-routines`: Claude Code routines or Codex scheduled tasks |
| Automations, and an SDK for building more bots | `setup-routines`, and trust-ladder's `orchestrate`, ported from the upstream orchestrate plugin to run Claude Code and Codex agents. The SDK plugin was left out; see below |
| Cloud agents | `setup-cloud-agents` |
| Automatically reproducing bug reports and opening pull requests | pstack's benny pack and the `reproduce-bugs` routine |
| pstack | `plugins/pstack`, vendored in full |

## Plugins in the kit

| Plugin | Skills | Why it is here |
|---|---|---|
| trust-ladder | 23 | This kit's own plugin: the ladder, lint packs, templates, the compat layer, and the skills for non-engineers. |
| pstack | 48 | The plugin the talk and both posts are about. Vendored with the principles, playbooks, agents, and the benny automation pack. `make-bot-ui` is left out: it builds pages for the upstream editor's Grok Bot. |
| team-workflows | 18 | pstack routes to its `control-ui`, `control-cli`, and `deslop`; the talk's CI and review workflow lives here. |
| thermos | 3 | The review panel team-workflows's `thermo-nuclear-code-quality-review` belongs to. |
| continual-learning | 1 | Turns transcripts into AGENTS.md updates: the rules layer learning on its own. Its cadence hook runs in Claude Code and Codex. |
| cli-for-agent | 1 | How to design the CLI a verification skill wraps, from Pt. 1's control-app. |
| agent-compatibility | 1 | Scores how agent-friendly a repository is; `trust-audit` uses it. |
| advisor | 1 | A second opinion before a risky step, from a fresh run of your own model. Its end-of-turn reminder runs in Claude Code and Codex. |
| teaching | 2 | Learning paths, so designers, marketers, and founders can build skills with agents. |

## Left out on purpose

From the upstream plugin repository:

| Plugin | Why |
|---|---|
| orchestrate (vendored) | Runs cloud agents through the upstream editor's SDK. trust-ladder's `orchestrate` skill is a port of it that runs Claude Code and Codex agents in the cloud or locally instead. |
| the SDK plugin | Documents the upstream editor's TypeScript SDK, which needs a paid account with it. Routines and the review workflows cover the bots this team builds. |
| ralph-loop | Claude Code's `/loop` and the faker-mode Autonomous run playbook do the same job. |
| create-plugin | Scaffolds plugins in the upstream editor's format; this kit ships Claude Code, Codex, and Pi manifests. |
| docs-canvas | Renders into the upstream editor's canvas; not referenced by the talk, posts, or pstack. |
| pr-review-canvas (standalone) | The same skill ships in team-workflows, which is included. |
| grok-voice | Voice features for Grok apps; unrelated to the trust ladder. |
| third_party connectors | MCP connector bundles for the upstream editor; Claude Code, Codex, and Pi connect to services their own way. |
